content: The text provided is a long list of references from various studies and articles related to visceral leishmaniasis, HIV co-infection, and associated treatments or outcomes. 1. Llach J, Boix V, Priego M, Merino E, et al. conducted a comparative study on visceral leishmaniasis in patients with and without HIV infection, published in Enfermedades Infecciosas y Microbiología Clínica in 1999. The study analyzed clinical outcomes and differences between these two patient groups. 2. Riera C, Fisa R, Lopez P, Ribera E, Carrió J, Falcó V, et al. evaluated the utility of a latex agglutination test (KAtex) for detecting Leishmania antigens in the urine of patients co-infected with HIV and visceral leishmaniasis. Their findings, published in the European Journal of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases in 2004, highlighted its diagnostic value and potential for post-treatment monitoring. 3. Ritmeijer K, Veeken H, Melaku Y, Leal G, Amsalu R, Seaman J, et al. investigated the equivalence of generic and proprietary sodium stibogluconate in treating Ethiopian visceral leishmaniasis. They also reported poor outcomes in HIV co-infected patients, as detailed in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2001. 4. Ritmeijer K, ter Horst R, Chane S, Aderie EM, Piening T, Collin SM, et al. assessed the limited effectiveness of high-dose liposomal amphotericin B (AmBisome) for treating visceral leishmaniasis in an Ethiopian population with high HIV prevalence. Their study, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2011, emphasized the challenges in managing co-infected patients. 5. Rosenthal E. explored the clinical characteristics of visceral leishmaniasis and HIV co-infection in southern France, as published in Presse Médicale in 1995. 6. Rosenthal E, Marty P, Poizot-Martin I, Reynes J, Pratlong F, Lafeuillade A, et al. further examined visceral leishmaniasis and HIV-1 co-infection in southern France, with findings published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1995. 7. Russo R, Nigro LC, Minniti S, Montineri A, Gradoni L, Caldeira L, et al. reported on the treatment of visceral leishmaniasis in HIV-infected patients using high-dose liposomal amphotericin B (AmBisome), as detailed in the Journal of Infection in 1996. 8. Salih NA, van Griensven J, Chappuis F, Antierens A, Mumina A, Hammam O, et al. evaluated the effectiveness of liposomal amphotericin B for complicated visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) in eastern Sudan. Their study, published in Tropical Medicine & International Health in 2014, addressed the challenges of treating this neglected disease. 9. Santos GO, De Jesus NPS Cerqueira-Braz JV, Santos VS, De Lemos LMD. investigated the prevalence of HIV and associated factors among visceral leishmaniasis cases in an endemic area of Northeast Brazil, as published in the Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical in 2019. 10. Silva de Lima UR, Vanolli L, Moraes EC, Ithamar JS, Pedrozo e Silva de Azevedo CDM. examined the impact of HIV on visceral leishmaniasis in Northeast Brazil, with findings published in PLOS One in 2019. 11. Silva-Freitas ML, Cota GF, Machado-de-Assis TS, Giacoia-Gripp C, Rabello A, Da-Cruz AM, et al. explored the link between immune activation, bacterial translocation, and frequent visceral leishmaniasis relapses in HIV-infected patients. Their study, published in PLOS One in 2016, highlighted the role of impaired immune recovery. 12. Singh S, Dwivedi SN, Sood R, Wali JP. analyzed the prevalence of hepatitis B, C, and HIV infections in multiply-injected kala-azar patients in Delhi, as published in the Scandinavian Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2000. 13. Singh S, Dahal P, Ngu R, Maguire B, Olliaro P, Stepniewska K, et al. conducted a systematic review to estimate the incidence rate of mortality for antileishmanial therapies, covering literature from 1980 to 2018. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2019. 14. Singh S, Kumar J, Singh R, Dwivedi SN. studied hepatitis B and C viral infections in Indian kala-azar patients receiving injectable antileishmanial drugs, as detailed in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2000. 15. Sinha PK, van Griensven J, Pandey K, Kumar N, Verma N, Mahajan R, et al. reported on the two-year treatment outcomes of liposomal amphotericin B for visceral leishmaniasis in HIV co-infected patients in Bihar, India. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2011. 16. Takele Y, Abebe T, Weldegebreal T, Hailu A, Hailu W, Hurissa Z, et al. investigated arginase activity in the blood of patients with visceral leishmaniasis and HIV infection, as published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2013. 17. Tavora LG, Nogueira MB, Gomes ST. evaluated the outcomes of visceral leishmaniasis/HIV co-infection in Northeast Brazil, as detailed in the Brazilian Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2015. 18. ter Horst R, Collin SM, Ritmeijer K, Bogale A, Davidson RN. examined the influence of antiretroviral treatment and other factors on outcomes in Ethiopian patients with concordant HIV and visceral leishmaniasis infections. Their study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2008. 19. Torre-Cisneros J. assessed the efficacy of liposomal amphotericin B in treating visceral leishmaniasis in HIV co-infected patients, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 1995. 20. Tortajada C, Pérez-Cuevas B, Moreno A, Martínez E, Mallolas J, García F, et al. demonstrated how highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) modifies the incidence and outcomes of visceral leishmaniasis in HIV-infected patients, as detailed in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2002. 21. Toumi A, Kilani B, Ammari L, Tiouiri H, Kanoun F, Belhadj S, et al. described the demographic, clinical, and therapeutic features of adult visceral leishmaniasis cases at Rabta Hospital in Tunis from 1983 to 2002, as published in the Bulletin de la Société de Pathologie Exotique in 2007. 22. Troya J, Casquero A, Muñiz G, Fernández-Guerrero ML, Górgolas M. explored the role of splenectomy in HIV-infected patients with relapsing visceral leishmaniasis, as published in Parasitology in 2007. 23. Vallejo A, Abad FM, Moreno S, Moreno A, Perez-Elias MJ, Dronda F, et al. investigated the immunological characteristics of HIV-1-infected patients with visceral leishmaniasis, focusing on CD4+ CTLA-4+ Treg cells and CCR5 density. Their findings were published in the European Journal of Clinical Microbiology & Infectious Diseases in 2014. 24. van Griensven J, Mengesha B, Mekonnen T, Fikre H, Takele Y, Adem E, et al. studied the predictive value of Leishmania antigenuria for treatment failure and relapse in visceral leishmaniasis/HIV co-infected patients in Ethiopia. Their exploratory study was published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology in 2018. 25. Villanueva JL, Alarcón A, Bernabeu-Wittel M, Cordero E, Prados D, Regordán C, et al. conducted a prospective evaluation and follow-up of European patients with visceral leishmaniasis and HIV-1 co-infection in the era of HAART, as published in the European Journal of Clinical Microbiology & Infectious Diseases in 2000.
